newsitem.title: USA: New NYC agency seen selling debt in August - Hevesi.
newsitem.headline: New NYC agency seen selling debt in August - Hevesi.

text.p: The New York City Comptroller predicted that a new borrowing arm for the city, which the legislature has approved but Gov. George Pataki still must authorize, would start selling debt as soon as August.
"Yes, sure," said Alan Hevesi, when asked on Wednesday whether this was a likely timetable in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. The interview will be shown on Thursday at 1515 EST.

The city comptroller explained that the exact breakdown between how much debt the new New York City Transitional Finance Authority would issue and how much general obligation debt the city would sell had yet to be finally determined.
Estimating the city sells from $4 billion to $3.8 billion of debt a year, Hevesi explained: "The gross would not change."

State lawmakers On Wednesday approved the legislation creating the new authority, which will be allowed to sell as much as $7.5 billion of bonds over four years, and Pataki has said that while he still has to read the bill, he is expected to sign it.

Developed to help the city get around its state-imposed debt cap -- which it is expected to hit around May -- the authority will lose its ability to issue debt once a constitutional amendment is approved that changes how this limit is calculated.

New York City's debt cap now is based on a five-year average of real estate prices, and the built-in lag means this measure does not fully reflect this sector's recovery since a sharp, local recession in the early 1990s.
